The bug is that disabling an endpoint appears to save, but the endpoint remains switched on.

The root cause is in `updateEndpoint`: the spread operator drops `false` when the endpoint is disabled, so the field never reaches the database. The enqueue logic already skips disabled endpoints, and the delivery job only checks for missing endpoints, not switched-off ones.

countEndpoints counts all endpoints, but createWebhook filters listEndpoints by enabled status.

The bug is a comment claiming only live endpoints consume the allowance. The fix is to use countEndpoints instead of filtering listEndpoints, since that helper was intended for quota checks.

Counting all endpoints makes the error message match the all-on case. Previously it reported only enabled usage, which was misleading.
Checking how other services count usage.

Three fixes are planned. The error message currently uses the filtered endpoint count, so tests snapshot "Plan growth allows 10 webhook endpoints" when all are enabled. Using `countEndpoints` instead will yield the same number.
